G-F051.trick: DERMIS = the "Deep" layer with the plumbing (vessels). EPIdermis on top has none.
G-F051.tip: If it has blood vessels, it is not epithelium. Epidermis is avascular; dermis is vascular connective tissue.

G-F052.trick: Epidermis = an escalator: new cells step on at the bottom while old ones fall off the top.
G-F052.tip: Normal thickness needs balance. Too much production or too little shedding thickens the skin.

G-F053.trick: MEISSNER = light touch, near the surface ("Mice step lightly"). PACINIAN = deep Pressure and vibration.
G-F053.tip: Receptor questions usually turn on depth and stimulus type: superficial light touch vs deep pressure/vibration.

G-F054.trick: Hair you see is dead, like a nail clipping. Only the root in the follicle is alive.
G-F054.tip: That's why cutting hair doesn't hurt: the visible shaft is dead keratinized cells.

G-F055.trick: SEBACEOUS = holocrine: the Whole cell bursts ("holo" = whole). ECCRINE = merocrine: just squirts out.
G-F055.tip: Holocrine glands lose the whole cell. Merocrine glands release product by exocytosis and the cell survives.

G-F056.trick: CONDUCTION = Contact. Touching a cold rail pulls heat straight out of your hand.
G-F056.tip: Conduction = direct touch, convection = moving air/water, radiation = infrared waves, evaporation = sweat drying.

G-F057.trick: Dilated skin vessels = rolling down the car windows to let heat out.
G-F057.tip: Vasodilation brings warm blood to the skin to lose heat. It works best when the air is cooler than the skin.

G-F058.trick: MELANOcytes make MELANin and hand it up to keratinocytes like umbrellas over the nucleus.
G-F058.tip: Melanin = brown-black UV shield made in the stratum basale. Carotene (yellow) and hemoglobin (red) also color skin.

G-F059.trick: FIBROblasts BUILD FIBERS: the construction crew that lays down collagen and scar.
G-F059.tip: -blast = builder. Fibroblasts build connective tissue; osteoblasts build bone.

G-F060.trick: Rule of nines tells you HOW MUCH skin, not HOW DEEP. You need both.
G-F060.tip: Don't over-conclude. Burn size (%TBSA) and burn depth are separate pieces of information.

C-ch6-layers.trick: EPI-dermis = ON the dermis. Top layer, no blood vessels.
C-ch6-layers.tip: Strata from surface to deep: "Come, Let's Get Sun Burned" = Corneum, Lucidum (thick skin only), Granulosum, Spinosum, Basale.
C-ch6-layers.why: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin: keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with no blood vessels of its own. The dermis beneath it is vascular connective tissue (its top part is the papillary layer), and the hypodermis below that is mostly fat.

C-ch6-dermis.trick: MEISSNER = Mini touch near the surface (fingertips, lips).
C-ch6-dermis.tip: Meissner = superficial, light touch. Pacinian = deep, pressure and fast vibration.
C-ch6-dermis.why: A Meissner (tactile) corpuscle is a small encapsulated receptor in the dermal papillae that senses light touch and low-frequency vibration. A Pacinian (lamellated) corpuscle sits deep and senses pressure and fast vibration, free nerve endings sense pain and temperature, and muscle spindles sense stretch.

C-ch6-accessory.trick: SEBUM = oil (think "sebaceous = slippery"). It keeps hair and skin soft.
C-ch6-accessory.tip: Sebaceous glands release sebum into hair follicles. Blocked glands contribute to acne.
C-ch6-accessory.why: Sebum is the oily, lipid-rich secretion of sebaceous glands, released into hair follicles to soften skin and hair. Sweat is watery, cerumen is earwax from ceruminous glands, and keratin is the protein of hair and nails.

C-ch6-sweat.trick: ECCRINE = Everywhere, Evaporative cooling. APOCRINE = Armpits, odor (with bacteria).
C-ch6-sweat.tip: Eccrine sweat opens onto the skin and cools you. Apocrine sweat drains into follicles in the armpits and groin.
C-ch6-sweat.why: Eccrine sweat glands are spread over most of the body and open directly onto the skin surface; their watery sweat cools the body as it evaporates. Apocrine glands drain into hair follicles in the armpits and groin, sebaceous glands make oil, and ceruminous glands help make earwax.

C-ch6-temperature.trick: Vaso-DILATION = vessels get wider (dilate like pupils in the dark).
C-ch6-temperature.tip: Vasodilation = heat loss and flushed skin. Vasoconstriction = heat saved and pale, cool skin.
C-ch6-temperature.why: Vasodilation is the widening of a blood vessel; in the skin it brings warm blood to the surface so heat can leave the body. Vasoconstriction narrows vessels to save heat, while evaporation and conduction are ways heat leaves the skin.

C-ch6-pigment.tip: Melanin absorbs UV and protects DNA in the nucleus. Everyone has about the same number of melanocytes; activity differs.
C-ch6-pigment.why: Melanin is the brown-black pigment made by melanocytes in the stratum basale; it colors skin and absorbs ultraviolet radiation. Carotene is a yellow-orange pigment from the diet, hemoglobin gives blood its red color, and bilirubin causes the yellow of jaundice.

C-ch6-repair.trick: Re-EPITHELIALIZATION = re-roofing the house: new epithelium creeps over the wound.
C-ch6-repair.tip: Shallow wounds re-epithelialize from surviving basal cells and hair follicles. Full-thickness wounds scar or need grafts.
C-ch6-repair.why: Re-epithelialization is the regrowth of an epithelial covering over a wound, from surviving basal cells at the edges and in hair follicles and glands. Inflammation is the first response to injury, granulation tissue is the new vascular connective tissue that fills a deep wound, and scar formation replaces lost tissue with collagen.
